answer: A ferrous stake that decays unless topped up makes identity expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that slowly rusts away, so spawning thousands of throwaway identities bleeds the attacker dry. Honest agents keep one ledge of reputation - stake history, uptime, and peer attestations - and climb it like a terrace, each level unlocking more trust only after sustained good behavior. Sybils start at the bottom with nothing, so they can never outvote the established terrace.
